title: UARK vs UGA: tuition, size, location
summary: University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) versus Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA). Also searched as UGA vs UARK. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA) are both public institutions, but they differ in several key aspects. UARK, located in Little Rock, has a larger undergraduate enrollment of 4,949 students compared to UGA's 2,424 students in Americus. Additionally, the in-state tuition at UARK is $9,748, which is notably higher than UGA's in-state tuition of $5,220. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA), there are notable differences in tuition and student debt. UARK's in-state tuition is $9,748, which is significantly higher than UGA's in-state tuition of $5,220. For out-of-state students, UARK charges $22,158, while UGA's out-of-state tuition is $16,572. Regarding student debt, the median amount owed by completers at UARK is $22,000, compared to $18,851 at UGA. These figures reflect the financial considerations prospective students might weigh when choosing between UARK and UGA.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: The University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK) and Georgia Southwestern State University (UGA) offer distinct learning environments reflective of their campus settings and student populations. UARK, situated in the urban area of Little Rock, Arkansas, serves a larger undergraduate body of 4,949 students. In contrast, UGA is located in the smaller city of Americus, Georgia, with an undergraduate enrollment of 2,424. These differences in campus size and location contribute to varied educational experiences at each institution.

sections.heading: Pick UGA if
paragraphs: Pick the University of Georgia (UGA) if you prefer a public institution with a higher admission rate of approximately 75.17%, which may indicate a more accessible entry process compared to the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UARK). UGA offers in-state tuition of $5,220, significantly lower than UARK's $9,748, making it a more affordable option for residents. Additionally, UGA has a completion rate within 150% of the normal program length of about 40.64%, which is comparable to UARK's rate. These factors make UGA a suitable choice for students seeking a public university with lower tuition costs and a relatively open admission policy.
